key_insight: Explicitly encoding salt preparation enabled interpretable machine-learning predictions of molten chloride corrosion, with the Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) emerging as the dominant descriptor.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support corrosion screening across alloys and molten chloride test conditions while providing uncertainty estimates.
method: Compile 291 literature-reported static corrosion experiments into a structured dataset.
Encode salt treatment, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurities using a graded CSPI.
Use a blended tree-based ensemble, sensitivity and SHAP analyses, and conformal prediction intervals.
evidence_signal: The ensemble achieved a cross-validated R² of 0.85 and MAE of 0.41 mg cm⁻² day⁻¹, with well-calibrated conformal prediction intervals reported.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to compiled static tests; generalization to flowing salts or unrepresented conditions requires validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
